Mr. President, on behalf of Brazil, I thank the Prosecutor for the briefing on the Court's twenty-sixth report and welcome the Permanent Representative of Libya. Complementarity remains a cornerstone of the Rome Statute: national jurisdictions hold the primary duty to prosecute, with the ICC acting only when a State is unable or unwilling. While Resolution 1970 (2011) recognizes that non-parties have no Statute obligations, Chapter VII mandates that Libyan authorities cooperate fully. Brazil welcomes the Office of the Prosecutor's strengthened cooperation with Libyan national authorities and notes the positive trajectory of recent engagements.

We urge all States and organizations to cooperate, as the ICC relies solely on States for enforcement. Requests must align with the Statute and relevant Council resolutions. Promoting accountability requires avoiding politicization and ensuring all victims of serious crimes are treated equally, regardless of the situation under investigation. Although no judgments have been rendered in the Libyan situation, we welcome the Office's evidence collection and investigative progress. To ensure transparency, we encourage the Prosecutor to provide additional information regarding his four key lines of inquiry.

Brazil hopes that a fruitful relationship between the Office and Libyan authorities will foster a culture of justice and accountability. We also welcome efforts to empower victims, witnesses, and affected communities inside and outside Libya, and encourage the Prosecutor to further engage with their representatives.<|im_end|>
